subject: General Knowledge
topic: Sobriquets and Nicknames of Famous Personalities

questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Iron Man of India'?

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru (first PM — 'Chacha Nehru', not Iron Man)
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (correct: Sardar Patel is called the Iron Man of India for his role in unifying princely states ✓)
Subhas Chandra Bose (Netaji — not Iron Man)
Bhagat Singh (Shaheed-e-Azam — not Iron Man)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is called the 'Iron Man of India' because of his firm and determined role in integrating 562 princely states into independent India. He was the first Deputy PM and Home Minister of India.

questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Nightingale of India'?

options.option_text: Indira Gandhi (first female PM — not Nightingale)
Lata Mangeshkar (Melody Queen/Nightingale of India ✓)
M.S. Subbulakshmi (Queen of Music — not Nightingale)
Asha Bhosle (singer but the Nightingale title belongs to Lata Mangeshkar)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Lata Mangeshkar is called the 'Nightingale of India' (also 'Melody Queen') for her incomparable voice and decades of contribution to Indian music. Note: Sarojini Naidu was called the 'Nightingale of India' in the context of poetry (in some contexts); but in music, it's Lata Mangeshkar.

questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru (architect of modern India, not the Constitution specifically)
Rajendra Prasad (first President of India — not the Constitution's father)
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (correct: Ambedkar chaired the Constitution Drafting Committee and is the principal architect of the Indian Constitution ✓)
Mahatma Gandhi (Father of the Nation — not specifically Constitution)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar is the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'. He chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and was the principal architect of the Constitution. He was also the first Law Minister of independent India.

options.option_text: Lal Bahadur Shastri (Man of Peace — not Frontier Gandhi)
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (correct: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan of the North-West Frontier Province is called Frontier Gandhi for his non-violent resistance ✓)
Vinoba Bhave (Acharya, social reformer — not Frontier Gandhi)
Jayaprakash Narayan (Loknayak JP — not Frontier Gandhi)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as Bacha Khan or Badshah Khan, is called 'Frontier Gandhi' because he advocated non-violent resistance in the North-West Frontier Province (now Pakistan) and was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Father of White Revolution' in India?

options.option_text: M.S. Swaminathan (Father of Green Revolution in India)
Verghese Kurien (correct: Verghese Kurien is the Father of White Revolution (Operation Flood / dairy development) ✓)
Norman Borlaug (Father of Green Revolution globally)
Amul (a brand/cooperative, not a person)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Verghese Kurien is called the 'Father of White Revolution (Milk)' and 'Milkman of India' for founding AMUL and launching Operation Flood — the world's largest dairy development programme. White Revolution = milk production revolution in India.

options.option_text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Ranade's disciple, moderate leader)
Bal Gangadhar Tilak (correct: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was given the title 'Lokmanya' (respected by the people) for his mass mobilisation work ✓)
Lala Lajpat Rai (Lion of Punjab — not Lokmanya)
Bipin Chandra Pal (one of Lal-Bal-Pal — not Lokmanya specifically)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was given the title 'Lokmanya' (accepted/respected by the people). He started Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivaji celebrations as public events to mobilise masses. Famous quote: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.' He was part of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio.

questions.stem: Who is known as 'Sparrow' in the world of cricket?

options.option_text: Sachin Tendulkar (Little Master/God of Cricket — not Sparrow)
M.A.K. Pataudi (Tiger — not Sparrow)
David Boon (The Keg — not Sparrow)
None of the above — this sobriquet does not belong to cricket commonly (correct: 'Sparrow' is not a well-known cricket sobriquet — the question tests awareness ✓)

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Sparrow' is not a common cricket sobriquet. Well-known cricket sobriquets: Sachin Tendulkar = Little Master/God of Cricket; Brian Lara = Prince of Trinidad; Kapil Dev = Haryana Hurricane; Sunil Gavaskar = Little Master; Rahul Dravid = The Wall; MS Dhoni = Captain Cool/Thala. This tests that students don't fall for unfamiliar sobriquets.

questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Astronomy'?

options.option_text: Brahmagupta (mathematician and astronomer, but Aryabhata is considered the Father)
Aryabhata (correct: Aryabhata (476–550 CE) is considered the Father of Indian Astronomy for his work Aryabhatiya ✓)
Varahamihira (astronomer, compiled Panchasiddhantika — but Aryabhata is the 'Father')
Bhaskaracharya (12th-century mathematician — after Aryabhata)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Aryabhata (476–550 CE) is the 'Father of Indian Astronomy'. In his work 'Aryabhatiya', he proposed that the Earth rotates on its axis, calculated the value of π to 4 decimal places, and made accurate calculations of solar and lunar eclipses.

options.option_text: Bhagat Singh (Shaheed-e-Azam — not Sher-e-Punjab)
Ranjit Singh (Maharaja Ranjit Singh who created the Sikh Empire — also called 'Lion of Punjab' ✓)
Lala Lajpat Rai (correct: Lala Lajpat Rai is also called 'Punjab Kesari' and 'Sher-e-Punjab' for his role in the independence movement ✓)
Sardar Beant Singh (Punjab CM, assassinated in 1995 — not the historical title)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Lala Lajpat Rai is called 'Sher-e-Punjab' and 'Punjab Kesari' (Lion of Punjab). He was one of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio and led protests against the Simon Commission in 1928. Note: Maharaja Ranjit Singh is also historically referred to as 'Lion of Punjab', but in independence movement context, it's Lala Lajpat Rai.

questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Missile Man of India'?

options.option_text: Homi J. Bhabha (Father of Indian nuclear programme)
Vikram Sarabhai (Father of India's space programme)
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (correct: Dr. Kalam is known as the Missile Man of India for his work on India's missile development programme ✓)
K. Sivan (current ISRO scientist — not Missile Man)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (1931–2015) is known as the 'Missile Man of India' for his pivotal role in developing India's missile technology under DRDO and ISRO. He also served as the 11th President of India (2002–2007). Notable missions: Agni, Prithvi, Trishul, Nag, Akash missiles.

options.option_text: Swami Vivekananda (Swamiji — not typically Gurudev)
Rabindranath Tagore (correct: Rabindranath Tagore is reverently called 'Gurudev'; Einstein called him 'the Great Sentinel' ✓)
Sri Aurobindo (Maharshi — not Gurudev)
Ramana Maharshi (Bhagavan Ramana — not Gurudev)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rabindranath Tagore is called 'Gurudev' (Divine Teacher). He wrote India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali. He founded Shantiniketan (now Visva-Bharati University).

questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution in India'?

options.option_text: Norman Borlaug (Father of Green Revolution GLOBALLY — won Nobel Peace Prize)
Verghese Kurien (Father of White Revolution/Milk — not Green)
M.S. Swaminathan (correct: Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is the Father of Green Revolution in India for introducing high-yielding wheat varieties ✓)
V.R. Krishna Iyer (jurist — not agriculture)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Dr. M.S. Swaminathan (1925–2023) is the Father of Green Revolution in India. He worked with Norman Borlaug to introduce high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice in India in the 1960s-70s, transforming India from a food-deficient nation to self-sufficient in grain production.
